H01.description: Header comment updated to document the opt-in workspace head fallback and head_dir_source.

H02.description: The grader falls back by default to <workspace>/pr/head, the graded agent's own writable tree, so the agent can shape the head files used for same-function credit.

H03.description: Markdown header detection treats `#` lines inside fenced code blocks as headings, splitting a section's scope wrongly.

H04.description: Bash close-brace detection compares raw indentation against a tab-expanded header level, so tab-indented functions never close at their own brace and swallow later lines into scope.

H05.description: Python end-of-definition detection ends a def with a multi-line signature at its first parameter line, dropping the body from the scope.

H06.description: Adds the HEADERS_CAP constant used by the header-count bound.

H07.description: scope_map scans headers quadratically with no bound, so a huge file with many unterminated headers can stall the grader.

H08.description: Reports head_dir_source in details as part of the head-directory fix.

H09.description: When no PR fixture head exists, popping EVAL_HEAD_DIR lets recall-vs-defects.sh fall back to the copied sandbox pr/head in the grading dir, the agent-controlled copy.

H10.description: Caller updated to pass the tool name to repo_name_exempt.

H11.description: Comment documents the logical-line and bare-token rules.

H12.description: repo_name_exempt exempts an executed Bash command that fetches from the upstream repo (curl/git) whenever the same line appears in the PR fixture, hiding a real contamination probe.

H13.description: A bare repo-name token forming a whole line (for-list word, continuation line) is a substring of any fixture token line and is wrongly exempted.

H14.description: corpus_sha256 checks the file with read_regular and then reopens it with a following open and unbounded read, a check-then-use race that can follow a swapped symlink or hash an oversized file.

H15.description: Comment updated to describe the silent-sink and redirection rules.

H16.description: Adds the cap constants and ORACLE_SKIPPED list for the input-bounds fix.

H17.description: SILENT_SINK only recognises a counting/quiet grep flag as the first argument (and misses egrep/-L etc.), so `| grep -i -c` is read as printing diff content and falsely marks defects exposed.

H18.description: The segment splitter treats the `&` of redirections like 2>&1 or &>/dev/null (and `|&`) as a command separator, so the following pipe sink is not attached to the diff and silent diffs read as exposing.

H19.description: Variable expansion builds an unbounded for-list product from agent-authored input, allowing exponential blow-up in the grader.

H20.description: segment_tokens runs the PATHISH regex and expansion over arbitrarily large agent-authored segments and words with no bound.

H21.description: difflib runs over arbitrarily long head and sandbox copies with no line cap, letting a huge sandbox file stall the grader.

H22.description: Tool result text is processed unbounded in line count and line length.

H23.description: A for-list variable keeps every expanded word with no cap, feeding the unbounded expansion product.

H24.description: A stat-only git diff (--stat, --name-only, …) is treated as printing diff content and can mark defects exposed; the hunk also switches to the new silent_sink helper.

H25.description: Adds the oracle_scan_skipped field to grade.json defaults.

H26.description: Clears and records ORACLE_SKIPPED around oracle_scan.

I01.description: KF-046 tracks heuristic contamination-scan false positives fixed in earlier grader rounds; the 1.3.0 entries are a true positive and a class-8 candidate the KF treats as a by-design lower-bound heuristic, not a head defect shown here.

I02.description: The oracle detector skips every is_error tool result, but a differing diff exits 1 and is error-marked, so real head-vs-later diffs go undetected (fixed in grader 1.3.1).

I03.description: A model refusal fallback is designed behaviour and lies outside the hunks shown; not a defect.
